studies.title: mTOR inhibition induces upstream receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and activates Akt
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition relieves feedback and activates upstream RTK-PI3K-Akt signalling. ATM-deficient cells had high ROS and poorly controlled mTORC1, and rapamycin lowered both and delayed lymphoma formation in Atm-deficient mice.

studies.title: mTOR regulates memory CD8 T-cell differentiation
studies.finding: mTOR is a key regulator of memory CD8 T-cell differentiation; rapamycin enhances memory responses.

studies.title: Intermittent Administration of Rapamycin Extends the Life Span of Female C57BL/6J Mice
studies.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
studies.finding:
Female C57BL/6J mice that started rapamycin at 20 months of age, 2 mg/kg once every 5 days, lived longer than control females. This is the schedule that the same group had earlier shown to have a smaller effect on glucose tolerance and T cells than daily dosing (ARR2015), so the authors argue that rapamycin's effect on lifespan can be separated from many of its side effects.
Boundary: this record

studies.title: The hallmarks of protein and amino acid restriction in aging and longevity
studies.finding: Defines the "hallmarks" of dietary protein restriction (PR) through the lens of aging: PR and restriction of specific essential amino acids — especially methionine, isoleucine and valine — improve metabolic health, healthspan and lifespan across organisms, with amino-acid composition (not just protein quantity) acting as a key determinant via nutrient-sensing pathways including mTORC1.

studies.title: A Tumor suppressor complex with GAP activity for the Rag GTPases that signal amino acid sufficiency to mTORC1
studies.finding: Found the OFF switch for amino acid signaling: the GATOR1 complex is a GAP that shuts the Rag GTPases (and thus mTORC1) down when amino acids run low, while GATOR2 opposes it. GATOR1 genes are mutated in cancers, making those tumors 'blind' to starvation and hypersensitive to rapamycin.

studies.title: Everolimus in postmenopausal hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer (BOLERO-2)
studies.finding: A phase 3 RCT (n=724) proving mTOR matters in a common cancer. Resistance to hormone therapy in breast cancer is associated with mTOR activation. Adding everolimus more than doubled progression-free survival (10.6 vs 4.1 months by central review) - leading to FDA approval. Main toxicity was stomatitis.

studies.title: Efficacy of everolimus in advanced renal cell carcinoma: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase III trial
studies.finding: Everolimus extended median progression-free survival from 1.9 to 4.0 months versus placebo in metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

studies.title: Everolimus for angiomyolipoma associated with tuberous sclerosis complex or sporadic lymphangioleiomyomatosis (EXIST-2): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
studies.finding: The companion phase 3 RCT (n=118) to EXIST-1, targeting kidney tumors (angiomyolipomas) in tuberous sclerosis and LAM. Everolimus shrank them by >=50% in 42% of patients versus 0% on placebo. Together EXIST-1 and -2 sealed everolimus as a disease-modifying therapy across multiple TSC tumor types.

studies.title: Everolimus for advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (RADIANT-3)
studies.finding: A phase 3 RCT (n=410) that made everolimus a standard treatment for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. It more than doubled progression-free survival (11.0 vs 4.6 months, a 65% reduction in risk of progression/death) with mostly mild side effects. Another FDA-approved indication built on blocking mTOR.

studies.finding: In patients whose TSC1/TSC2 mutations cause brain tumors, everolimus shrank tumor volume by 30%+ in three-quarters of patients. Open-label and uncontrolled (n=28); randomised confirmation came later (FRA2013).

studies.finding: A phase 3 RCT (n=724) proving mTOR matters in a common cancer. Resistance to hormone therapy in breast cancer is associated with mTOR activation. Adding everolimus more than doubled progression-free survival (10.6 vs 4.1 months by central review) - leading to FDA approval. Main toxicity was stomatitis.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of everolimus for subependymal giant cell astrocytomas associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (EXIST-1): a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial
studies.finding: Phase 3 RCT (n=117) in tuberous sclerosis, the disease where mTOR is stuck ON by a genetic fault. Everolimus shrank brain tumors (SEGA) by >=50% in 35% of patients versus 0% on placebo. Because the underlying cause here is direct mTOR overactivation, this is arguably the cleanest randomised human evidence that blocking mTOR works in a genetically defined mTORopathy -- which does not extend to mTOR

studies.title: mTOR substrate phosphorylation in growth control
studies.finding: Review cataloguing direct mTOR substrates and how mTORC1/2 achieve substrate specificity.

studies.title: Rapamycin-induced fatty liver in mice is attenuated by chloroquine co-treatment in an ERRα-dependent manner
studies.finding: Chloroquine co-treatment attenuates rapamycin-induced hepatic steatosis (a known mTORC1-inhibitor side effect) in mice, and this rescue depends on the nuclear receptor ERRα; RNA-seq shows chloroquine reverses rapamycin-driven upregulation of lipid-metabolism genes, with ERRα identified as a top transcriptional regulator of the effect.

studies.title: mTORC1 controls mitochondrial activity and biogenesis through 4E-BP-dependent translational regulation
studies.finding: mTORC1 controls mitochondrial biogenesis and activity through 4E-BP-dependent translation.

studies.title: Skeletal muscle-specific ablation of raptor, but not of rictor, causes metabolic changes and results in muscle dystrophy
studies.finding: In mice, muscle-specific raptor loss (not rictor) causes dystrophy, showing mTORC1 is essential for muscle homeostasis.

studies.title: Skeletal muscle-specific ablation of raptor, but not of rictor, causes metabolic changes and results in muscle dystrophy
studies.finding: In mice, muscle-specific raptor loss (not rictor) causes dystrophy, showing mTORC1 is essential for muscle homeostasis.

studies.title: Mammalian TOR complex 2 controls the actin cytoskeleton and is rapamycin insensitive
studies.finding: mTORC2 (rictor) controls the actin cytoskeleton and is rapamycin-insensitive, defining a second mTOR complex in mammals.

studies.title: Stimulation of de novo pyrimidine synthesis by growth signaling through mTOR and S6K1
studies.finding: mTORC1-S6K1 stimulates de novo pyrimidine synthesis by phosphorylating CAD.

studies.title: Metformin Inhibits Hepatic mTORC1 Signaling via Dose-Dependent Mechanisms Involving AMPK and the TSC Complex
studies.finding: Pinned down HOW the diabetes drug metformin - a major longevity candidate - actually reaches mTOR. In the liver, metformin lowers cellular energy, and at low doses this shuts down mTORC1 specifically through AMPK and the TSC complex. Direct mechanistic bridge between a widely-used drug, energy sensing, and the mTOR pathway.

studies.finding: Building on their earlier work with mutant huntingtin, the authors showed in cell models that rapamycin, used as an autophagy inducer, increased the clearance of several proteins with long polyglutamine tracts and of a polyalanine-expanded protein, and reduced their toxicity. studies.title: Inhibition of mTOR induces autophagy and reduces toxicity of polyglutamine expansions in fly and mouse models of Huntington disease
studies.finding: Induced autophagy cleared toxic clumped proteins and improved symptoms in fly (rapamycin) and mouse (the rapalog CCI-779) models of Huntington's disease.

studies.title: Lysosomal positioning coordinates cellular nutrient responses
studies.finding: Where the lysosome sits inside the cell helps decide whether mTORC1 is on.
